references.text: Explains why Gideon was given the name Jerub-Baal, which means 'let Baal contend against him,' because he tore down Baal's altar. Abimelek was the son of Jerub-Baal (Gideon).
States that Gideon's concubine in Shechem bore him a son whom he named Abimelek. This is the background for Abimelek mentioned by Ga'al.
Describes how Abimelek gained support from the people of Shechem through his mother's family, which Ga'al now challenges.
Introduces Ga'al son of Ebed, who came to Shechem and won the trust of the city's men, providing the context for his challenging speech.
Mentions Hamor, Shechem's father, who was the leader of the Hivites. Ga'al refers to Hamor's men as the original inhabitants of Shechem.
States that Jacob bought the plot of land at Shechem from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father. This establishes Hamor's historical connection to the city.
